prompt: You told a coding agent "add team accounts" and it built something plausible but nothing like what customers asked for.
tells: nothing like what customers asked for
why: Write a short spec (users, flows, rules, why) before asking for code.
trap: Checking afterwards catches it late; the gap was up front.

prompt: A feature will touch billing, permissions and the UI over two weeks of agent sessions.
tells: touch billing, permissions and the UI
why: A written spec is the shared reference every session starts from.
trap: A plan says how; the spec says what and why, first.

prompt: Product, design and engineering each pictured a different "export" feature, and the agent built a fourth.
why: Agree on one written spec before anyone (or any agent) builds.
trap: Clarifying questions help, but the output must be a shared spec.

prompt: You want a quick spike to see whether a charting library can render 1 million points. Writing a full spec first would mostly slow you down. Which practice are you choosing to skip?
why: Spec-first pays off for real features; for a throwaway experiment, skipping it is reasonable.
trap: Know when the practice isn't worth it.
